script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only: a competitive game, not a assigned favorite. Minnesota has leaned on Aaron Jones (35 carries, 145 yards in weeks 1-2) with Jordan Mason (15/59) mixing in, but Tampa allows 3.26 YPC and only 4 runs of 10+, so that run lean stalls and the MIN passing game (Jefferson 16 targets, 171 air yards; the rusher log lists Wentz 5/8, not Murray) has to work against a 49% blitz. Tampa can stay in it because Minnesota blitzes 78% and Mayfield's EPA is +0.02 vs blitz (n=14) versus -0.33 unblitzed, with Bucky Irving (25/134 rush, 11 targets, -47 air yards) as the rush-plus-checkdown engine.
script.flip1: Tampa's 3.26 YPC run defense and 49% blitz put Minnesota behind early, Jones's carries fall off the 17.5/game pace toward a Mason split, and Jefferson/Hockenson have to throw into the middle (TB allows 12.4 YPA there, but only on 10 attempts) while Irving's rush stalls and only checkdowns keep his scrimmage line alive.
script.flip2: Minnesota's 78% blitz and middle bleed (10.58 YPA, 9 passes of 20+ on 84 attempts) let Tampa lead and run clock: Irving's carries hold or rise, Gainwell still does not become a feature, and Minnesota abandons Jones so the MIN rush overs die.

edge_players.kills_it: Irving is scratched or limited (inactives were not in the pack) and Gainwell inherits the 12-carry plus checkdown role, or one screen/explosive clears 32 by itself.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Irving is at 91.5 rush+rec yards per game (134 rush, 49 rec on 11 targets and -47 air yards) against 77.5, and Minnesota's 78% blitz plus 8 runs of 10+ allowed is the environment for those checkdowns and chunk runs to continue.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot be priced against a sharp book. Form agrees: Gainwell 16.5 vs 32; Irving 91.5 vs 77.5. A hostile rush-only check (12.5 carries times MIN 3.85 YPC = 48, plus 24.5 rec = 72.5) sits under 77.5, but a 50/50 blend of his 5.36 and that 3.85 is about 57.5 rush plus 24.5 rec = 82, still over, and the 78% blitz is a reason receiving does not shrink. That is not a clean disagree, so the lean is not dropped. Nothing here is a 70%+ model probability.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the two-game roles were a mirage: Irving was on a snap count or out, Gainwell took 14 touches for 40-plus scrimmage yards and cleared 32, and Irving finished near 50 rush and 15 receiving. Or both played, Minnesota sold out on the back after film of 5.36 YPC, the checkdowns went to Cade Otton (already 11 targets, 64 yards), and one Gainwell screen still beat 32 in a pass-heavy flip. Spread and weather were never in the pack, so a blowout or a wind/rain slog could have cut Irving's rush without a pre-kickoff tell.

Jones rush over 52.5 (72.5 recent; about 57 even at TB's 3.26 YPC if 17.5 carries hold, -112) is a separate MIN-volume idea that dies if Minnesota trails, so it stays off this slip.
